subject: zoology_2
question_text: Explain the mechanism by which HIV multiplies and leads to AIDS.

mark_split.label: What HIV is and how it spreads

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.37, SAQ 30. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. steps.label: What HIV is
steps.why: The virus attacks the very cells that organise the immune response, so the defence itself is what fails.
common_mistakes: Writing that HIV spreads by touch or by air. It does not.
Confusing HIV, the virus, with AIDS, the condition.
steps.memory_tip: HIV is the virus; AIDS is what it finally causes.
steps.margin_note: Full form, then the routes of spread.
lines: HIV means Human Immunodeficiency Virus.
It spreads by sexual contact, by blood
transfusion, by sharing needles with an
infected person, and from an infected
mother to her child.

steps.label: Entry and reverse transcription
steps.why: The virus carries RNA but the host works in DNA, so it must copy its RNA backwards into DNA before anything else can happen.
common_mistakes: Writing that HIV carries DNA. It carries single stranded RNA.
steps.memory_tip: RNA to DNA is backwards, so the enzyme is reverse transcriptase.
lines: After entering the host, HIV enters the TH
cells, macrophages and dendritic cells.
Its single stranded RNA makes a DNA strand
complementary to the viral RNA, using the
enzyme reverse transcriptase.
The same enzyme makes a second DNA strand,
so double stranded viral DNA is formed.

steps.label: The provirus
steps.why: Once the viral DNA is inside the host's own DNA, the cell copies it as if it were its own, and there is no way to remove it.
common_mistakes: Leaving out integrase, the enzyme that inserts the DNA.
steps.memory_tip: Integrase integrates it; the inserted DNA is the provirus.
steps.margin_note: Name the enzyme and the inserted DNA.
lines: The viral DNA is put into the host DNA by
the enzyme integrase.
The inserted DNA is called the provirus.
The provirus makes RNA, which is
translated into viral proteins.
These particles are assembled into new HIV.

steps.label: Destruction of TH cells
steps.why: Each infected cell turns into a factory and is destroyed making virus, so the count of helper cells falls until infections cannot be resisted.
common_mistakes: Writing that symptoms appear at once. They may take months to ten years.
Leaving out the destruction of TH cells.
steps.memory_tip: The helper cells become factories, then die.
steps.margin_note: End with the time gap and the symptoms.
lines: The infected human cells act as HIV
generating factories.
The TH cells are infected and destroyed.
The time between infection and the first
symptoms may be a few months to 10 years.

lines.text: Symptoms: fever, diarrhoea and loss of weight

insider_note: Reverse transcriptase and integrase are the two enzymes the question is really asking about. Name both, with the step each one performs.
